The concept is pretty interesting, but mostly I just see untapped potential. A whole lot more could've been done within the framework and mechanics the devs came up with, but the game is marred with mediocre acting and subpar writing. These sorts of experiences are made or broken by the quality of the text they offer, and this one lost its twist, its atmosphere and any potentially emotional connection with the characters to cheesy, melodramatic writing.

While I can't vouch for my adult self to like this game as much as I did when I was a kid, I remember this game being genuinely one of the scariest games I'd ever played. That's probably not saying a ton, though, since I can't make it through a lot of the big-name horror games like Amnesia, uhhh the other ones, etc. Usually for me, psychological thriller type stuff spooks me a lot and this game kept me and my friend HOOKED.

Had a lot of fun. I have never played FMV game. So I was unsure if I was gonna like it. But it was such an unique experience for me. Even the progression of the game or story, finding clues, I have never played such a game.

The story is that you found a random phone. After opening the phone, you realize that the phone belongs to Anna who is at the moment missing. So now you are trying to help to find her along with some of other people. And if exclude the horror elements, I really felt like it's an actual event, I felt like I was interacting with real people doing simple but realistic things to find this missing person.

Simulacra is a horror graphic / text adventure (I don't know how else I could define it). 

Story and Characters, two main characteristics of the genre, are really weak. What bothered me the most, though, was the interface and the gameplay. Players only use during the whole game Anna's smartphone and mess with her social media accounts, messages and so on, in order to find out what happened to her. I feel like we already spend way too much time using these technologies and social media, so I didn't enjoy this experience so much.

You may find this concept interesting, though. In this case the game is worth the price, since there are several endings and Easter Eggs to be discovered in multiple runs (I got only a couple of them, though).

It really depends on how much you share my opinion, whether you should buy this game or not. If you feel that the mentioned aspects may annoy you, you'd better use your money and time in other games. Otherwise you can give Simulacra a try.

This is a very acclaimed horror game for its unique format, solving a mystery remotely through a victim's cell phone. And for that I was very interested! And those elements I was looking for, it delivered.

I do have other issues, though. While I feel like this is creepy and atmospheric set-up that would lend itself well to horror scenarios like a serial killer or modern hauntings, I wasn't as grabbed by the big bad revealed in the climax [spoiler]what with the more SciFi twist with commentary on a modern person's internet persona vs their true selves, especially since there seemed to be at least some vague supernatural ability given to this system that is never expanded upon[/spoiler]. Though, with the very apparent and similar themes to this series' free-to-play title [i]Simulacra: Pipe Dreams[/i] which I have completed previously, I'm not sure what else I expected.

These games are cheap enough, with gimmicky-enough gameplay and good enough atmosphere that doesn't overstay its welcome with a pretty short playtime that I overall still really like it. The way the live action footage is used to weave a narrative was iconic for the time, after all, to where upon release I saw people playing this everywhere. I'd say I'm just happy enough to say that not only did I enjoy this game but I'm interested in what became of the next couple of games.

But note: I also couldn't get this game working for the longest time - I bought it forever ago and just got it to work on the day I'm writing this. It was missing some kind of runtime package that another game's install eventually provided. So keep that in mind. That was a pain.

I'm gonna recommend the game because there's not many out there like this, so I hope more get made. 

HOWEVER, the acting is pretty subpar - not Wendy Van Horen's (who plays Anna), not even Denise Chan's (Ashley). Everyone else though... there is a reason why Greg's first voice message became a literal meme for years on Jacksepticeye's channel. 

Aside from the acting, they really need an editor. Not sure if whoever wrote this knows English as a second language (I hope so), but the amount of poor grammar mistakes is astounding. 

And don't tell me they're to set the mood, because if I have to suspend my disbelief about random people sharing all the private information you ask for willy nilly, then you have to suspend yours about believing proper grammar exists.

I enjoyed playing through this different kind of horror game as it provided a new experience. It's fun to slowly uncover things and unlock new pieces of the puzzle as you progress while trying to solve the mystery.

There is a first time for everything, it seems. In this case, it is digging through someone's phone to find out more about her life, connections, steps and what happened to her. Never have I ever done this before.
Anna is the missing woman's name and we get our hands on her phone. As an outsider, we are supposed to find her by solving nice puzzles. The outcome of this game seems to be heavily dependent on the choices the player makes, which are mostly the answers to dialogues and steps one takes. Even in the first playthrough, I did not need any guide to solve the puzzles, which is nice. Some were challenging enough to delay the end of the game a little bit. Multiple endings give you the possibility to replay the game and see, what different answers and a different playstyle will lead to.

Simulacra is a found phone horror game with cutscenes that is only fun once. I really wish I could give this a medium review as it is not entirely bad...


Aesthetics:
I gotta say the aesthetics are  a bit dated. It pretty much screams early 2010 but the horror aspect is still pretty good! The acting in the cutscenes is okay but not the best.

Story:
Premise of a haunted found phone is pretty cool. The story is alright but the characters are getting super annoying pretty fast and are just not that believable to be honest. The puzzles are okay but the game really, really drags on and on. Yes, there are multiple endings but when you are done with one ending you don't really feel like seeing the others...
Also the good endings are achieved by not being a decent human being?
The horror aspect gets lost due its sideplots and the climax was actually ... not scary but just weird?

Gameplay:
Puzzle solving. You try to retrive data from her phone and really invade her privacy to be honest. At first it is interesting but I felt pretty bad trying to go really personal stuff of hers.

The game that pioneered the "found phone" genre. For some reason this genre hasn't caught on as much as I'd expected it to by now (2023), which is a shame as it is the perfect vehicle for a modern horror adventure game. I hope one day to see it developed past the sparse, awful and grindy "free" games that drag out and lose focus (Duskwood etc) and are essentially your only other options after finishing this series, which itself is not what I would consider the best this genre could offer if done properly (but it's a good start!). As it is though, there's really nothing else out there so if you find the genre as enjoyable as I did, you won't have anywhere else to go afterwards.
